hunts_questions.name: audit_logs chain extends correctly across 2 refund events?
hunts_questions.evidence: Each refund path writes its OWN audit_logs row via the frozen-zone AuditLogService::write API (HMAC SHA-256 chain-signed, prev_hash → current_hash, append-only via DB BEFORE DELETE trigger that SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' on MySQL prod). Subcase (a) cashier path: PaymentService.php:155-169 writes 'payment.cash_back_issued' with payload {order_serial_no, transaction_id, transaction_no, payment_method, amount, fiscal_sequence_no}. Subcase (b) counter-entry path: RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:301-316 writes 'order.refund.counter_entry' with payload {parent_order_id, parent_serial_no, parent_fiscal_sequence_no, mirror_fiscal_sequence_no, mirror_total, mirror_payments_count, reason}. Webhook path: Stripe.php:417-430 writes 'order.refunded.stripe_dashboard' with payload {order_id, charge_id, amount_refunded, source, webhook_id, sealed_note}.
hunts_questions.3way_concurrency_analysis: All three writes funnel through AuditLogService::write which uses Cache::lock + DB FOR UPDATE on the chain head (frozen-zone NF525-critical service per CLAUDE.md §7). The lock serializes the writes — they extend the chain sequentially even when initiated concurrently. Each write computes prev_hash from the current head, sets its own current_hash, and atomically advances the chain pointer. Result: in the 3-way race (cashier + webhook), TWO distinct audit_logs rows are appended (one from cashier path, one from webhook path) — chain extends correctly, no gap, no corruption, no race condition on prev_hash because of the Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE serialization. Both rows are forensically captured and queryable for reconciliation.
hunts_questions.z_report_correctness: ZReportService::aggregate sums orders.total + order_payments per mode in the Z window. Subcase (a) cashier path mutates parent.payment_status=REFUNDED but does NOT create a mirror Order → orders.total query picks up the parent at +N (not netted). HOWEVER, in subcase (a), the cashier called CANCEL → status transitions BEFORE the Z close, the order is excluded from the Z aggregation via status filters in ZReportService (orders with status=CANCELED are not aggregated as taxable sales). Subcase (b) counter-entry creates a mirror with negated total + negated order_payments → Z nets to 0 correctly (proven by RefundMirrorSplitPaymentTest::test_refund_z_reconciliation_under_credits_zero_after_fix). Webhook path: does NOT create a mirror — IF parent is pre-Z mutable, Persist listener flips parent.payment_status=REFUNDED but parent.total stays unchanged in orders → Z over-counts revenue if parent is still in the window. POST-Z parent: per Stripe.php:391-409 a 'sealed_parent' note is logged; mirror must be created manually via RefundWithCounterEntryService — V1.0.2 backlog.
hunts_questions.verdict: VERIFIED for audit chain extension (Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE serialization). ATTENTION on Z aggregation: webhook-triggered pre-Z refund flips payment_status but does NOT net the total — see L8.2-NEW-2 P1.

hunts_questions.subcase_b_curl_counter_entry: ONE fresh fiscal_sequence_no allocation via FiscalSequenceService::next($branchId) at RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:103 INSIDE the same DB::transaction as the mirror Order create. Cache::lock 5s + DB FOR UPDATE = triple defense (per CLAUDE.md §8). Monotonic per branch, gap-free invariant preserved. Webhook path (subcase b interleaving): STILL zero allocations — webhook does NOT create mirror. So total: ONE new fiscal_sequence_no per refund (from the counter-entry path only).
hunts_questions.what_if_webhook_did_create_mirror_v102: V1.0.2 backlog plan to wire webhook → mirror creation would need to call FiscalSequenceService::next from within Stripe.php — concurrent with the cashier subcase (b) calling next() from RefundWithCounterEntryService. FiscalSequenceService::next is frozen-zone with Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE — proven concurrent-safe per CLAUDE.md §8 'triple defense'. Two concurrent next() calls would serialize → two distinct sequential fiscal_sequence_no values allocated → one for each mirror. BUT also need UNIQUE(parent_order_id) to block the second mirror Order::create — first wins, second hits SQLSTATE 23000 → caller catches at PosOrderController.php:81-96 → 409 MIRROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. The second fiscal_sequence_no would be allocated but UNCONSUMED (gap-free invariant violated). MITIGATION REQUIRED for V1.0.2: gate fiscal_sequence allocation behind a parent_order_id existence-check in the same tx, OR move the UNIQUE check before next(). Currently V1 webhook does NOT create mirror — so this gap is theoretical, NOT live.
hunts_questions.verdict: VERIFIED for V1 shape — subcase (a) + webhook = 0 new sequences; subcase (b) + webhook = 1 new sequence. The hypothetical V1.0.2 webhook-creates-mirror would need ordering re-design to preserve gap-free invariant under concurrency — see L8.2-NEW-3 P1 backlog.

new_findings_p0_p1_p2.title: OrderPaymentStatusChanged broadcast fires TWICE in cashier + webhook 3-way race — different correlation_id → distinct outbox rows
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.evidence: PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedOnRefundCreated.php:128-138 dispatches OrderPaymentStatusChanged INSIDE try/catch but OUTSIDE the lockForUpdate envelope (lines 89-109). Both listener invocations (cashier RefundCreated + webhook RefundCreated) reach this dispatch site even after one of them short-circuits at line 98-100 (because the early-return is INSIDE the closure passed to DB::transaction; the dispatch at line 125 still executes). PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox.php:33-39 idempotency_key = sha1(EventType|orderId|oldPaymentStatus|newPaymentStatus|correlationId). The cashier request and the webhook request enter the application via SEPARATE HTTP requests with SEPARATE correlation_id (request-scoped UUID per PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox.php:120-136 — falls back to fresh Str::uuid() when neither Log::sharedContext nor X-Correlation-ID header carries a value). Different correlation_id → different sha1 → firstOrCreate returns wasRecentlyCreated=true on BOTH calls → TWO DomainEvent rows → TWO DispatchDomainEventsJob → TWO broadcasts to private-branch.{branch_id}.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.impact: NOT data corruption — both broadcast payloads carry the same payment_status=REFUNDED, the UI re-render is idempotent (same DOM state). Potential UI flash if the listener handler isn't debounced on the client side (PosOrdersTrackerComponent / KdsComponent / OssComponent). The DomainEvent table accumulates 1 extra row per 3-way race occurrence (negligible — 3-way race is rare per task framing 'RARE cascade'). NF525 audit chain unaffected (audit_logs receives one row per path, NOT one per broadcast).
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.double_check_inner_short_circuit: Re-read PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedOnRefundCreated.php:76-83: the OUTER short-circuit at lines 81-83 fires when (int)$order->payment_status === REFUNDED on the in-memory Order model. BUT: each listener invocation receives a DIFFERENT $order Eloquent instance (cashier's RefundCreated::dispatch passes the cashier's loaded model; webhook's RefundCreated::dispatch passes the webhook's loaded model). Each in-memory model was loaded BEFORE the other's mutation committed. So both pass the line 81 check with oldPaymentStatus != REFUNDED. The INNER short-circuit at line 98-100 fires correctly (lockForUpdate sees the committed REFUNDED), but it short-circuits the SAVE inside the tx — NOT the dispatch at line 125 which is outside the tx closure. Confirmed: TWO dispatches reach the outbox.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.fix_v1_0_2: Three options of increasing scope: (a) MIN: gate the dispatch at line 125 by reloading $order or checking $locked.payment_status (requires refactor to hoist $locked out of the closure or set a post-tx flag). (b) MEDIUM: extend outbox idempotency_key to include a refund-event-correlation field — e.g. add an originating-refund-event-uuid that BOTH cashier and webhook RefundCreated emit so the second outbox write dedups. (c) MAX: short-lived Cache::lock keyed on (orderId, REFUNDED) in the Persist listener so only one broadcast wins per N seconds. Defer to V1.0.2 — V1 race is rare AND broadcast is idempotent UI-side per current FoodKing client patterns.

new_findings_p0_p1_p2.title: Webhook-triggered pre-Z refund flips payment_status=REFUNDED but does NOT net orders.total — Z over-counts revenue if parent stays in current window
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.evidence: Stripe.php:318-445 charge.refunded branch dispatches RefundCreated which fires PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedOnRefundCreated. The listener at lines 87-109 (mutable path) mutates parent.payment_status=REFUNDED but does NOT mutate parent.total, does NOT create a mirror Order with negated total, does NOT touch order_payments. ZReportService::aggregate (per K.5 hunt K5.10 reference) sums orders.total in the Z window — the parent at +N stays in the sum (not netted). For an order created and refunded WITHIN the same Z window, this is a P1 NF525 risk: Z reports total revenue HIGHER than what Stripe actually paid out.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.subcase_b_protection: Counter-entry path (RefundWithCounterEntryService) DOES create a mirror with negated total + negated OrderPayments → Z nets correctly (RefundMirrorSplitPaymentTest::test_refund_z_reconciliation_under_credits_zero_after_fix). But the counter-entry path is GATED on SealedOrderGuard::assertSealed — only fires post-Z. For PRE-Z refunds, the V1 contract is: use the pre-Z RETURNED path which DOES net via standard order_status transitions + the standard OrderStatusChanged cascade. The webhook bypasses both.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.subcase_a_protection: Cashier cancel-with-reason path → OrderService::changeStatus(CANCELED) → ZReportService excludes canceled orders. NETS correctly via status filter. Webhook does NOT transition status to CANCELED — only flips payment_status=REFUNDED. Status stays at whatever the parent had (DELIVERED, PREPARING, etc.) → Z still includes the order.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.impact_severity: P1 fiscal drift if Stripe dashboard refunds are issued on orders within the current Z window. V1 operational mitigation: instruct owner to refund FROM POS UI only (cancel-with-reason or post-Z curl refund-with-counter-entry), NEVER Stripe dashboard. K.8 K8-F-03 V1.0.2 backlog already calls out this requirement: 'V1 operations doc instructs owner to refund FROM POS UI only, never Stripe dashboard, until V1.0.2 cascade lands.' The K2-HEAL-04 shipped the BROADCAST + AUDIT side but did NOT close the Z-aggregation side.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.fix_v1_0_2: Either (a) webhook path triggers a mirror creation for pre-Z orders (status-aware: pre-Z = standard RETURNED path via OrderService::changeStatus; post-Z = RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute) — requires fiscal-sequence-allocation under webhook concurrency (L8.2-NEW-3 ordering concern), (b) webhook path additionally calls ZReportService::recomputeForRefund(orderId) or similar to invalidate the cached Z aggregation. CONFIRM with operator that the V1 carrying-over of K8-F-03 V1.0.2 backlog item ALSO covers Z-aggregation — current K.8 wording focuses on cascade gap and ledger divergence but the Z-drift was implicit.

new_findings_p0_p1_p2.category: fiscal sequence allocation ordering under concurrency
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.title: If V1.0.2 wires webhook → automatic mirror creation, fiscal_sequence_no allocation must precede UNIQUE(parent_order_id) check to preserve gap-free invariant
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.evidence: RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:101-130 current order: (1) FiscalSequenceService::next allocates at line 103, (2) Order::create with parent_order_id at line 108-125, (3) save with fiscal_sequence_no at line 127-130. The UNIQUE(parent_order_id) constraint fires at step 2 — if a concurrent transaction already inserted a mirror for this parent, step 2 throws SQLSTATE 23000. BUT step 1's fiscal_sequence_no has ALREADY been allocated and incremented (Cache::lock + FOR UPDATE on the per-branch counter). The 23000 throws → outer DB::transaction rolls back → fiscal_sequence_no rollback semantics depend on FiscalSequenceService implementation. If next() uses Cache::lock to claim + DB UPDATE to persist + the OUTER tx rollback discards the UPDATE → sequence is RETURNED (gap-free preserved). If next() commits the increment in its OWN sub-tx independent of the outer (e.g. uses DB::transaction internally with autoCommit semantics) → sequence is CONSUMED but unattached to any order row → gap-1 violates gap-free invariant.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.verification_needed: Read app/Services/Fiscal/FiscalSequenceService.php (frozen-zone, NF525-critical per CLAUDE.md §7) to confirm whether next() participates in the caller's tx or commits independently. THIS IS OUT OF L.8.2 read-only scope (file is frozen-zone) — defer to a dedicated audit task. If next() commits independently, then current V1 single-caller path (only RefundWithCounterEntryService calls next from refund context) is safe because the second caller is blocked by UNIQUE BEFORE reaching next()... ACTUALLY no, next() is called FIRST. So even in V1 single-caller path, if two concurrent counter-entry curls hit the same parent: cashier A's next() allocates seq=42, cashier A's Order::create inserts mirror, COMMIT. Cashier B's next() allocates seq=43, cashier B's Order::create hits UNIQUE 23000, ROLLBACK. Seq=43 status depends on next() semantics. If FiscalSequenceService commits independently → seq=43 is consumed and gap-free invariant violated.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.actual_v1_protection: V1 has TWO defenses against concurrent counter-entry: (1) IdempotencyKeyMiddleware caches the SECOND request keyed on (branch_id, user_id, hash(X-Idempotency-Key)) — typical cashier UI uses ONE idempotency key per logical refund attempt → second request returns the cached 2xx response without re-entering the service. (2) DB UNIQUE(parent_order_id) blocks the second mirror Order::create. The race window where (1) fails (different idempotency keys, different cashiers) AND (2) fires is small but non-zero. If V1 operates with single-resto + low concurrent refund volume → 0 observed occurrences expected. POST V1.0.2 webhook-creates-mirror: webhook handler runs WITHOUT IdempotencyKeyMiddleware (Stripe webhook bypasses the middleware via CSRF except + middleware chain in stripe.php route file lacks the middleware) → defense (1) gone → only defense (2) remains. The fiscal_sequence_no gap risk activates.
new_findings_p0_p1_p2.fix_v1_0_2: When wiring webhook → mirror creation (V1.0.2): (a) acquire a row-level lock on parent BEFORE calling next() so a concurrent counter-entry call serializes on the parent (lockForUpdate inside a SELECT for the parent), (b) check existence of (parent_order_id, status=RETURNED) mirror BEFORE next(), (c) wrap next() + Order::create in a single DB::transaction so a UNIQUE collision rolls back the sequence consume. Or: ensure FiscalSequenceService::next ALWAYS participates in the caller's outer tx (not a sub-tx) so rollback semantics preserve gap-free. RECOMMEND a frozen-zone audit gate to verify next() tx semantics before V1.0.2 webhook bridge ships.
